question: Does replacing the universal star/gas morphology mixture by each cluster's independently measured central BCG and gas masses make the P0557 angular tensor more consistent?

locked_field.lineage: P0557 exact-selection result; no coupling or operator is refit here

mass_anchor_rule.stellar_mass: published BCG total stellar mass with 10 percent uncertainty
mass_anchor_rule.gas_mass: published cumulative Chandra gas mass within the listed 14.3-22.2 kpc aperture and its published uncertainty
mass_anchor_rule.mixture: f_gas = k_gas*Mgas/(Mstar+k_gas*Mgas); combine separately normalized registered star and X-ray morphology maps with weights 1-f_gas and f_gas
mass_anchor_rule.interpretation: measured per-object baryonic input, not a gravity parameter
mass_anchor_rule.known_mismatch: Mstar is a BCG total while Mgas is aperture cumulative; the registered F160W map also contains satellites/ICL, so this is a mass-anchor proxy rather than a complete surface-density map

spent_data_disclosure: All four systems and the t=0.3 contrast choice are spent from prior work. P0558 is a fully specified diagnostic, not fresh validation.
claim_limits: The central gas and BCG stellar masses do not constitute radial two-dimensional component mass maps.
X-ray brightness and its square root remain morphology proxies.
The four systems are spent, so the result is diagnostic even though the rule is frozen before this score.
Galaxy and Solar preservation remains by external-environment scope.
